newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to expand foreign ceiling in index futures.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to expand foreign ceiling in index futures.

text.p: South Korea's finance and economic ministry said on Wednesday it would expand a foriegn investment ceiling in index futures to 30 percent of average daily open interest in the previous three trading months from November 1.
The ceiling is currently at 15 percent.
The limit for individual foreign investors outside the country will be raised to 5.0 percent, effective November, from 3.0 percent presently.
South Korea began futures trading for the first time on May 3 by launching the KOSPI-200 index based on the largest 200 companies listed on the Korea Stock Exchange.
But the market's trading volumes remain low and few investors are using the KOSPI 200 for arbitrage.
Foreign investors have largely avoided the index futures market due to tight trading restrictions, analysts said.

"As we launched the index futures for the first time in May, we tried to operate it in a conservative way. But there has been a lot of demand to raise the ceiling because it is not enough to hedge investment risks," said a finance ministry official.
Under the previous limit, foreign investors invested only 60 billion won in index futures while spending 1.7 trillion won in the local spot market.
The official said he expected a further $15 million would flow into the market under the ceiling expansion.
In October, South Korea raised the foreign investment ceiling in the cash market to 20 percent from 18 percent.
